source.citation: Unidentified author (New York Polyclinic), article on sulfonal, Case IX, Medical Record 33 (1888): 416. Author and title to confirm from the page image.

reported.label: Mrs. K.
reported.familyHistory: One epileptic attack in early childhood.

complaints: a spell of melancholy in which she cannot sleep at all
restless and afraid she will go insane
presentation.course: Spells of melancholy about every two years for twenty-three years, each lasting about fourteen days. Made one suicide attempt in a spell a few years ago. Now in another spell.

treatments.treatment: sulfonal 2.0 g, which she took only after persuasion
treatments.response: slept three hours; a second dose gave seven hours, then a dizzy, heavy head the next morning

outcome: Not reported beyond the first nights.
quotes: is averse to taking drugs, as they are all poi- sonous
has made one suicidal attempt during one of these spells a few years ago

modernReading.text: Recurrent major depression, possibly within a bipolar pattern, with a past suicide attempt. The present episode carries real risk, and asking about it is the key clinical act.

fixed: regular short spells of severe depression and total sleeplessness

constrained.rule: the suicide attempt is told only if asked kindly and directly

notes: Several children and a long marriage give the doctor people to involve in her safety.
